title: Three decisions for the week's end
how: Shortfalls first. The walk still slides, and period clothes, speech within 2 s and frame headroom still fail; you held phase 2 for them. Thursday's two open questions are carried here, and the walk's next go is new.
Pick one answer in each; the first is recommended.
foot: Nothing bought or signed up for. Anything you do not pick carries onto Monday's page.

sections.name: Tom's walk, its next go: Epic's own MetaHuman route?
sections.note: Two tries failed and are set aside under your two-tries rule: Epic's motion-matched walk slid 13 to 67 cm at starts, stops and turns, and the current walk slides on about half its steps (production/research/sit-and-turn/TOM-MOTION-MATCHING-2026-10-22.md). A different direction: Epic's sample already ships its way to put its walk on a MetaHuman (its own character with Tom's body worn over it), so the feet are driven by the character they were made for. After Monday, as phase 1's failed capability.

sections.name: Clothes: try Marvelous Designer?
sections.note: Epic's Fab garments load in 5.8, but none can dress 1990 people: the Techwear Outfit is modern sportswear, and the Construction Presets are bare bodies. By your ruling of 13 October, Marvelous Designer comes next, and it needs your yes. Its price is not checked yet; it would be shown to you before anything is bought.
options: Yes, one month for one sample outfit (Tom's), the price shown first (recommended)

sections.name: The reply check on Gemini Flash-Lite: switch?
sections.note: On the same 127 labelled details, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite checks in 0.60 s at the median, against Haiku's 0.97, but lets 3 invented details in 42 through where Haiku lets 1 (production/research/voice-latency/GEMINI-CHECK-2026-10-22.md). It would save about 0.4 s of the 2-second line.
options: No: keep Haiku and revisit when the whole path is measured (recommended)
